nodes.content: Design a network diagnosis system that separates concurrent causal faults from downstream symptoms under asymmetric routing and incomplete telemetry.
requirements: Achieve ≥90% fault-localization precision at ≥80% incident coverage with 30% telemetry loss.
Report observationally indistinguishable fault sets without asserting unsupported single-cause explanations.

nodes.content: Build a forward/reverse-path causal factor graph with joint fault inference, symptom-propagation factors, missingness-aware likelihoods, and indistinguishable-fault-set reporting.
Which forward/reverse-path evidence distinguishes simultaneous link faults from propagated symptoms under 30% probe loss?
Forward/reverse path divergence and interface counters distinguish concurrent faults from propagated symptoms at ≥90% precision, ≥80% coverage under 30% loss.
Replay AsymFault-30 dual-fault and symptom-only incidents with directional probes, interface counters, and 30% dropout; measure localization precision and coverage.
On AsymFault-30 at 30% dropout, directional probes plus counters achieved 92% fault-localization precision and 83% incident coverage.
Adopt directional probes and interface counters for joint fault inference; AsymFault-30 exceeds both targets despite 30% dropout.
Implement the adopted probe-and-counter factor graph, report indistinguishable fault sets, and validate precision and coverage on held-out AsymFault-30.
Implement PathGraph v1 with direction-specific probe/counter factors, symptom-propagation edges, dropout-aware joint inference, and observational-equivalence reporting.
PathGraph v1 exposes directional factor-graph inference, missing-telemetry likelihoods, and equivalence-class fault reports without unsupported single-cause attribution.
Run PathGraph v1 on held-out AsymFault-30 with 30% dropout; measure precision, coverage, equivalence-set recall, and unsupported singletons.
Held-out AsymFault-30 at 30% dropout yielded 87% precision and 82% coverage; shared-interface symptoms caused false fault labels.
Condition shared-interface counters on fanout; independent directional evidence and fault-set abstention yield ≥90% precision, ≥80% coverage at 30% loss.
Test fanout-conditioned PathGraph v2 with fault-set abstention on untouched AsymFault-30 incidents at 30% dropout; measure precision and coverage.
On untouched AsymFault-30 with 30% dropout, PathGraph v2 achieved 92% precision, 81% coverage, and zero unsupported single-cause reports.
Ablate fanout conditioning and directional probes on AsymFault-30 at 30% dropout; measure precision, coverage, and unsupported singleton rate.
On AsymFault-30’s separate ablation cohort, full PathGraph v2 reached 88% overall precision at 81% coverage; both ablations worsened precision.
Stratum-calibrated shared-interface likelihoods and directional-probe gating yield ≥90% precision at ≥80% coverage across cohorts with 30% dropout.
Calibrate PathGraph v3 on training strata; test precision, coverage, and unsupported singletons across held-out cohorts with 30% dropout.
At 30% dropout, PathGraph v3 achieved ≥91% precision and ≥80% coverage in each held-out cohort, with zero unsupported singletons.
Stress-test PathGraph v3 on topology-shifted AsymFault-30 incidents with correlated 30% telemetry loss; measure precision, coverage, and false singletons.
Topology-shifted AsymFault-30 with correlated 30% loss yielded 86% precision, 77% coverage, and four unsupported singletons for PathGraph v3.
Topology-aware path uncertainty and correlated-dropout modeling with fault-set abstention achieve ≥90% precision and ≥80% coverage under shifted, 30%-loss telemetry.
Run factorial topology-shift × dropout-correlation ablations on PathGraph v3 at 30% loss; measure precision, coverage, and unsupported singletons.
Factorial ablations: shifted topology with independent 30% loss retained 91% precision, 80% coverage, and zero unsupported singletons.
Implement PathGraph v4 with uncertain-route marginalization, correlated-dropout factors, and fault-set abstention; evaluate shifted AsymFault-30 at 30% loss.
On shifted AsymFault-30 with correlated 30% loss, PathGraph v4 reached 93% precision but 76% coverage; zero unsupported singletons.
Deploy v3 only under validated independent-loss conditions; defer correlated-loss v4 despite zero unsupported singletons until coverage reaches 80%.
Add budgeted adaptive bidirectional probes targeting ambiguous fault sets during correlated outages, retaining set-valued reports until evidence separates causes.
Can four adaptive bidirectional probes per incident restore ≥80% coverage at ≥90% precision under correlated 30% loss?
Entropy-ranked bidirectional probes separate ambiguous fault sets within four probes per incident, raising shifted-cohort coverage to ≥80% without lowering precision.
Simulate four entropy-ranked bidirectional probes per incident with PathGraph v4 on shifted AsymFault-30 under correlated 30% loss.
On shifted AsymFault-30, four adaptive probes raised PathGraph v4 coverage from 76% to 82% at 92% precision; zero unsupported singletons.
Implement entropy-ranked probing atop PathGraph v4, then validate the four-probe budget and set-valued reporting on held-out correlated-loss incidents.
Implement ProbeSelector v1 with entropy-ranked forward/reverse probes, four-probe incident caps, and fault-set-preserving PathGraph v4 integration.
ProbeSelector v1 schedules up to four entropy-ranked directional probes per incident and updates PathGraph v4 fault-set posteriors.
Replay held-out correlated-loss AsymFault-30 through ProbeSelector v1 and PathGraph v4; measure precision, coverage, probe counts, and unsupported singletons.
Held-out correlated-loss AsymFault-30: ProbeSelector v1 achieved 91% precision, 81% coverage, zero unsupported singletons, averaging 3.2 probes per incident.
Stress-test ProbeSelector v1 against shared-conduit probe blackouts and mid-incident asymmetric reroutes; measure precision, coverage, and unsupported singletons.
Under shared-conduit blackouts and asymmetric reroutes, ProbeSelector v1 yielded 88% precision, 73% coverage, and two unsupported singletons.
How can adaptive probes avoid shared-conduit blackouts and stale asymmetric routes while preserving valid fault-set ambiguity?
Conduit-disjoint probe selection plus route-epoch invalidation restores ≥90% precision and ≥80% coverage under blackouts and reroutes without unsupported singletons.
Compare conduit-disjoint, route-epoch-aware ProbeSelector v2 against v1 under blackouts and reroutes; measure precision, coverage, and unsupported singletons.
Blackout/reroute replay: ProbeSelector v2 achieved 91% precision, 80% coverage, zero unsupported singletons versus v1’s 88%, 73%, and two.
Ablate conduit diversity and route-epoch invalidation separately on held-out blackout/reroute incidents; measure precision, coverage, and unsupported singletons.
Held-out blackout/reroute cohort: full v2 yielded 92% precision, 77% coverage, zero unsupported singletons; route-epoch ablation produced two.
Deploy four-probe ProbeSelector v1 only for validated correlated-loss incidents; retain v2’s route-epoch safeguards but defer blackout/reroute deployment pending ≥80% coverage.
Fuse time-aligned BGP updates, optical alarms, and sampled flows using route-epoch causal inference and ambiguity-preserving fault sets.
Can route-epoch-aligned BGP, optical alarms, and sampled flows restore blackout/reroute coverage without mistaking downstream symptoms for faults?
Route-epoch-aligned BGP and optical alarms plus sampled flows raise blackout/reroute coverage to ≥80% at ≥90% precision without unsupported singletons.
Replay held-out blackout/reroute incidents with 30% telemetry loss; compare epoch-aligned BGP, optical, and flow fusion against ProbeSelector v2.
At 30% loss, full fusion reached 89% precision and 82% coverage; misaligned optical alarms caused three unsupported singletons.
Stratify fusion errors by BGP route epoch, optical alarm skew, and flow sampling rate; measure precision, coverage, and unsupported singletons.
With optical alarm skew ≤2 seconds, epoch-aligned fusion achieved 92% precision, 81% coverage, and zero unsupported singletons.
Enable fusion only when optical skew ≤2 seconds; otherwise preserve ambiguous fault sets rather than risk misaligned-alarm singletons.
Build skew-gated route-epoch fusion, then validate fault-set precision, coverage, and singleton safety across mixed-skew blackout/reroute incidents.
Implement EpochFuse v1 with ≤2-second optical-skew gating, route-epoch joins, sampled-flow factors, and set-valued fallback for untrusted alarms.
EpochFuse v1 joins BGP and sampled-flow evidence by route epoch, gates optical alarms at ≤2-second skew, and preserves fault-set ambiguity.
Replay mixed-skew blackout/reroute incidents at 30% telemetry loss through EpochFuse v1; measure precision, coverage, and unsupported singletons.
Mixed-skew blackout/reroute replay at 30% loss: EpochFuse v1 achieved 91% precision, 80% coverage, and zero unsupported singletons.
Adopt skew-gated EpochFuse v1 for blackout/reroute incidents; mixed-skew replay meets both targets without unsupported single-cause reports.
